assay_type: Cellular concentration-response viability/growth assay using ATP luminescence
system: Mouse BaF3 cells expressing recombinant human AXL (P30530); include parental/vector-control BaF3 cells if available
readout: CellTiter-Glo ATP luminescence as a surrogate for viable cell number/metabolic activity, normalized to vehicle/untreated controls

steps.instruction: Prepare AXL-expressing BaF3 cells and controls; plate a compound dilution series with matched vehicle, untreated, background, and if available parental/vector-control cells.
steps.parameters: cell_density: unresolved; medium: unresolved, use validated BaF3 culture medium and keep IL-3/growth-factor conditions constant across arms; top_concentration_uM: 30 (provisional assumption, not sourced); dilution_factor: 3 (provisional assumption); n_points: 8 (provisional assumption); replicates: 3 (provisional assumption); vehicle_fraction: match top compound concentration, assumed <=0.3% v/v DMSO (provisional assumption)

steps.instruction: Expose cells to compound and controls under standard culture conditions; include a vehicle-only arm and untreated arm.
steps.parameters: exposure_time: 72 h (provisional assumption, not sourced); temperature: 37°C (provisional assumption); CO2/humidity: unresolved, use standard cell-culture conditions

steps.instruction: Apply CellTiter-Glo ATP viability reagent, mix, stabilize, and measure luminescence according to a validated vendor/lab procedure.
steps.parameters: reagent_volume: unresolved; mix_time: unresolved; stabilization_time: unresolved; follow validated CellTiter-Glo procedure and keep detection timing constant across plates

steps.instruction: Normalize luminescence to vehicle/untreated controls, subtract background, fit a concentration-response curve, and report uncertainty and assay limitations.
steps.parameters: fit_model: four-parameter logistic with variable Hill slope (provisional assumption); acceptance_criteria: unresolved numeric thresholds; require acceptable vehicle/background signal, monotonic dose-response where possible, and report confidence intervals; do not report an IC50 if the curve is incomplete or poorly constrained

controls: Vehicle-only control with matched DMSO fraction
Background control: medium plus detection reagent without cells
Reference AXL inhibitor/positive control: unresolved and not supplied in packet
rationale: The question asks about growth/proliferation or viability of BaF3 cells expressing recombinant human AXL, so the cellular ATP viability template is appropriate; biochemical kinase cards would measure enzyme inhibition, not cellular viability. A broad dilution series and replicates are needed to estimate a cellular concentration-response. This design can establish whether CHEMBL4845957 reduces BaF3-AXL viability/growth under the tested conditions, but ATP viability alone does not establish AXL target engagement, kinase inhibition, or target-specific causality. The numeric concentration series, exposure time, and replicate count are provisional design assumptions because the packet provides no retained measurement examples or source-supported values.
limitations: No retained measurement examples or source-supported assay parameters are provided; top concentration, dilution factor, n_points, replicates, exposure time, and vehicle fraction are provisional assumptions, not sourced facts.
ATP-based viability cannot distinguish cytostasis from cytotoxicity and does not measure AXL kinase activity directly.
A viability effect in BaF3-AXL cells does not establish target-specific causality; off-target toxicity or medium/growth-factor effects remain possible.
Parental/vector-control BaF3 cells and a validated reference AXL inhibitor are needed to assess AXL dependence; the reference control is unresolved in the packet.
Cell density, medium composition, IL-3/growth-factor status, reagent volumes, mixing/stabilization times, and acceptance thresholds are unresolved and must be set from validated lab procedures.
This design does not predict a withheld IC50 and cannot establish biochemical inhibition of Tyrosine-protein kinase receptor UFO.
